newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Effects of Swedish CPI change unknown - Riksbank. [CORRECTED 20:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Effects of Swedish CPI change unknown - Riksbank. [CORRECTED 20:36 GMT]

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Tuesday it was too early to draw any conclusions from calculation changes in the Swedish consumer price index.

Sweden's official data bureau Statistics Sweden said earlier on Tuesday that from April 1997 it would change its method of calculating the consumer price index and revised its March figures upwards baced on the new procedure.
It also said that when April consumer price index data is published on May 15 at 0715 GMT, the release will include revised figures for the period from January 1995 to March 1997.

The changes were being made because in the past, household interest costs for the repayment of property loans were undervalued, Statistics Sweden said. "We won't know the scenario until May 15 when the revised CPI statistics are presented. We will publish a new inflation report in one month," Jonas Ahlander, head of the Riksbank's division for price analysis, told Reuters.
"Today I can not say anything about what conclusion we will draw in it," said Ahlander.
The statistics office (corrects source from the Riksbank) revised one figure, saying the year on year rate of inflation in March was unchanged instead of showing a fall of 0.4 percent.
